chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Sa'd ibn Zarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said in his hadith until he reached the Mosque of Kufa, which was built with pottery, bricks, and clay. He said: Woe to the one who demolished you! Woe to the one who facilitated your demolition! Woe to the one who built you with solid bricks, changing the Qibla of Nuh! Good fortune to the one who witnesses your demolition with the Qaim of my Ahl al-Bayt! Those are the best of the nation with the righteous of the 'Itrah.

key_terms.قَائِمُ أَهْلِ بَيْتِي: The Qaim (Raiser) of my Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the construction and demolition of the Mosque of Kufa?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological significance of the Mosque of Kufa, linking its physical state to the era of the Mahdi (al-Qaim). The mention of altering the Qibla of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of identifying the 'Qibla of Nuh' as the Kaaba in Mecca, suggesting that the reconstruction with bricks involved a shift in prayer orientation or architectural grandeur that distinguished it from the original simplicity. The promise of 'good fortune' (tubba) to those witnessing its demolition alongside the Mahdi underscores the concept of *shahada* (witnessing) as a key virtue in the final days of the Prophet's lineage.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 495 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ali bin Hakam from Rabi bin Muhammad Musli from Saad bin Tareef from Asbagh bin Nubatah

that Amirul Momineen (a.s) said in his speech regarding the Kufa Masjid that it was made from mud, bricks and clay. Then he said: “When Qaim (a.s) reaches the Kufa Masjid, its walls would be of solid bricks and mortar; he would look at it and say: Woe be on the one who demolished you, woe be on the one who facilitated your razing, and woe be on the one who constructed you with solid bricks and changed the Qibla of Nuh. And fortunate are those who witness the razing in the company of the Qaim of Ahle Bayt. They are the best of the peoples.”
